title: The Night Market
learning_objectives: Read a longer story independently and follow one character's feelings
Find evidence for how a character feels
parent_prompts: Let the child read alone. After: how did Sam feel at the start, and at the end? Which words told you?

pages.text: Sam had never been to the night market. When the sun went down, Dad said, "Coat on. We are going." Sam's tummy did a small flip.
pages.illustration_brief: Sam pulling on a coat in a doorway at dusk; Dad waiting with a torch.
pages.audio_script: Sam had never been to the night market. When the sun went down, Dad said, Coat on. We are going. Sam's tummy did a small flip.
pages.image_alt: Sam pulling on a coat in a doorway at dusk; Dad waiting with a torch.

pages.text: The street was strung with lights, red and gold. Music came from somewhere. So many people! Sam held Dad's hand tightly and stayed close.
pages.illustration_brief: A street with strings of lanterns; a crowd; Sam pressed against Dad's side.
pages.audio_script: The street was strung with lights, red and gold. Music came from somewhere. So many people! Sam held Dad's hand tightly and stayed close.
pages.image_alt: A street with strings of lanterns; a crowd; Sam pressed against Dad's side.

pages.text: A man was making sugar into shapes over a small fire. A fish. A dragon. A bird. Sam stopped, and forgot to be nervous.
pages.illustration_brief: A vendor pouring golden sugar into a bird shape on a board; Sam watching wide-eyed.
pages.audio_script: A man was making sugar into shapes over a small fire. A fish. A dragon. A bird. Sam stopped, and forgot to be nervous.

vocabulary.definition: A little bit scared or worried about what will happen.
vocabulary.example: I feel nervous before a test.

pages.image_alt: A vendor pouring golden sugar into a bird shape on a board; Sam watching wide-eyed.

pages.text: "Which one?" the man asked. Sam pointed at the bird. It came on a stick, thin as glass and warm.
pages.illustration_brief: Sam holding a golden sugar bird on a stick up to the lantern light.
pages.audio_script: Which one? the man asked. Sam pointed at the bird. It came on a stick, thin as glass and warm.
pages.image_alt: Sam holding a golden sugar bird on a stick up to the lantern light.

pages.text: Further on, a woman played a wooden flute. Children clapped. Sam let go of Dad's hand to clap too.
pages.illustration_brief: A flute player under lanterns; children clapping; Sam clapping with both hands, Dad beside.
pages.audio_script: Further on, a woman played a wooden flute. Children clapped. Sam let go of Dad's hand to clap too.
pages.image_alt: A flute player under lanterns; children clapping; Sam clapping with both hands.

pages.text: They shared a paper cone of hot corn. They watched a boy spin a top the size of a plate. Sam did not want to go home.
pages.illustration_brief: Sam and Dad sharing corn; a big spinning top on the ground in front of a boy.
pages.audio_script: They shared a paper cone of hot corn. They watched a boy spin a top the size of a plate. Sam did not want to go home.
pages.image_alt: Sam and Dad sharing corn; a big spinning top on the ground in front of a boy.

pages.text: On the way back, the lights got smaller behind them. Sam's tummy did another flip, but a happy one this time.
pages.illustration_brief: Sam and Dad walking away, the lit market small behind; Sam looking back smiling.
pages.audio_script: On the way back, the lights got smaller behind them. Sam's tummy did another flip, but a happy one this time.
pages.image_alt: Sam and Dad walking away, the lit market small behind; Sam looking back smiling.

pages.text: "Same time next week?" asked Dad. Sam nodded so hard the sugar bird nearly fell off its stick.
pages.illustration_brief: Sam nodding hard; the sugar bird wobbling on its stick; Dad laughing.
pages.audio_script: Same time next week? asked Dad. Sam nodded so hard the sugar bird nearly fell off its stick.
pages.image_alt: Sam nodding hard; the sugar bird wobbling on its stick; Dad laughing.

quiz.prompt: How did Sam feel at the start of the market?
quiz.explanation: Sam's tummy did a flip (page 1) and Sam held Dad's hand tightly and stayed close (page 2). Those are signs of feeling nervous.

quiz.prompt: What made Sam forget to be nervous?

options.text: Watching the man make sugar shapes

quiz.explanation: Page 3: Sam stopped to watch the sugar shapes, and forgot to be nervous.

quiz.prompt: What shows that Sam felt braver later?

options.text: Sam let go of Dad's hand to clap

quiz.explanation: On page 2 Sam held Dad's hand tightly. On page 5 Sam let go to clap. That change shows more confidence.

quiz.prompt: What did Sam and Dad share?
quiz.explanation: Page 6: They shared a paper cone of hot corn.

quiz.prompt: Tell a grown-up how Sam's feelings changed from the start to the end, and what changed them.
quiz.rubric: not yet: says Sam went to a market; with support: nervous then happy, with prompting; independent: nervous at first (tight hand), the sugar shapes and music helped, happy at the end and wants to go again
quiz.explanation: Tracking a feeling across the story with evidence is the target skill.

activities.claim: Sam was nervous at the start.
activities.prompt: Which page gives the best clue?

off_screen_prompt: Draw two faces: how Sam felt at the start and at the end. Tell someone what changed.
